statutes.title: What considerations and objects are lawful, and what not
statutes.summary: Agreements whose object or consideration is forbidden by law, defeats provisions of law, or is regarded as immoral or opposed to public policy are void.
statutes.authority: Supreme Court of India / High Courts
statutes.remedy: The clause is ab initio void and unenforceable before any court of law.

statutes.title: Agreements in restraint of legal proceedings, void
statutes.summary: Every agreement by which any party is restricted absolutely from enforcing their rights by the usual legal proceedings in ordinary tribunals, or which limits the time to enforce rights, is void to that extent.
statutes.remedy: Citizens cannot be barred by a contract from approaching civil courts or consumer forums.

statutes.title: Compensation for breach of contract where penalty stipulated for
statutes.summary: When a contract is broken, if a sum is named as penalty, the party complaining is only entitled to receive reasonable compensation not exceeding the amount named, and cannot levy punitive or unconscionable forfeitures.
statutes.remedy: Forfeiture must represent genuine pre-estimated loss; unearned entire security deposit confiscation is illegal.

statutes.title: Unfair Contract Terms
statutes.summary: A contract with a consumer having terms that cause significant change in consumer rights, such as requiring excessive security deposits, imposing unreasonable penalty, unilateral termination without reasonable cause, or refusing early termination.
statutes.authority: District / State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (DCDRC)
statutes.remedy: Consumer Commission has statutory power to declare unfair contract clauses null and void.

statutes.act: Model Tenancy Act, 2021 / State Rent Control Acts
statutes.title: Ceiling on Security Deposit & Restrictions on Eviction
statutes.summary: Security deposit for residential premises cannot exceed two months' rent. Landlord cannot evict tenant without following due legal notice procedure and cannot unilaterally cut off essential supplies (water/electricity).
statutes.authority: Rent Authority / Rent Court / Rent Tribunal
statutes.remedy: Landlord cutting essential services or seizing premises is punishable with statutory penalties and restoration orders.

statutes.title: Entry of Landlord into Premises with Prior Written Notice
statutes.summary: Landlord or property manager cannot enter premises without at least 24 hours prior written notice (or electronic message) and entry must be between 7:00 AM and 8:00 PM.
statutes.remedy: Unannounced entry is a violation of privacy and constitutes civil trespass.

statutes.act: RBI Master Direction – Fair Practices Code for Lenders
statutes.title: Code of Conduct for Recovery and Prohibition of Harassment
statutes.summary: Recovery agents shall not resort to intimidation, harassment (verbal or physical), calling borrowers before 8:00 AM or after 7:00 PM, contacting borrowers' phonebook contacts, or threatening criminal arrest for debt default.
statutes.authority: RBI Ombudsman / Banking Lokpal / Consumer Commission
statutes.remedy: File immediate complaint on RBI CMS (sachet.rbi.org.in); criminal FIR under BNS 351/IPC 506 for criminal intimidation.

statutes.title: Punishment for cheating by personation by using computer resource
statutes.summary: Whoever by means of any communication device or computer resource cheats by personation (e.g., posing as Court, Police, CBI, ED, or RBI) shall be punished with imprisonment up to 3 years and fine.
relevance_keywords: pay to UPI to avoid arrest
statutes.authority: Cyber Crime Police Station / National Cyber Crime Portal (1930 / cybercrime.gov.in)
statutes.remedy: Immediately report to 1930; do not remit any funds; legal notices from Indian Courts never demand instant UPI transfers.

statutes.title: Rights of Allottees and Return of Amount with Interest
statutes.summary: If builder fails to give possession in accordance with terms, buyer is entitled to claim full refund with interest or monthly interest compensation till possession.
statutes.remedy: File petition before State RERA for refund with prescribed SBI MCLR + 2% interest rate.

statutes.title: Criminal Intimidation
statutes.summary: Threatening injury to person, reputation or property with intent to cause alarm is a criminal offence punishable with imprisonment.
relevance_keywords: threatening to ruin credit score illegitimately
statutes.remedy: Lenders cannot use physical threats or goons. Register police complaint immediately.
